Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

grave noun

a burial place

also tomb, burial place

classical

Cic. Leg. 2.57 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 323

sepulcrum, sepulcrī n.

noun, second declension

grave, tomb

Any burial place, from sepelīre, to bury.

Other words

  • tumulus, tumulī m. — a grave mound

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 5.42: tumulum facite

    Properly a mound of earth (see mound).

  • monumentum, monumentī n. — a tomb, a memorial

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Vulg. Mt. 27.60: posuit illud in monumentō suō novō; Cic. Mil. 17 (Lewis & Short)

    The Vulgate’s word for the tomb of Christ.

Examples

  • saeptum undique et vestītum vepribus et dūmētīs indāgāvī sepulcrum

    I tracked down the tomb, fenced in on every side and overgrown with brambles and thicketsCic. Tusc. 5.64

See also cemetery, funeral, monument, mound.

SourcesLewis & Short: sepulcrum · Lewis & Short: tumulus · Lewis & Short: monumentum
